title: Adoption plan / run-summary delta
description: Delta to 001's run-summary.schema.json for the adopt command (FR-024). Two changes there: the `command` enum gains "adopt", and an `adoption` property carries the object defined here. The DEFAULT output stays human-readable prose; this JSON form is the opt-in --json output, and MUST be byte-identical between the Bash and PowerShell ports for identical inputs (SC-008). The same object is the --dry-run report, which is why FR-023's 'identical action set' is a structural guarantee rather than a behavioural promise.

enabled.description: The effective value of adoption.enabled. False means the run refused at the enablement gate with zero reads against candidate tickets (FR-001).

label_prefix.description: The validated prefix every searched label was built on (FR-002). A prefix, never a credential or a host (FR-025).

confirmed.description: True when the apply phase ran (--yes, or an interactive confirmation). False for a dry-run, a decline, and the no-terminal-without---yes path — in all of which the plan is identical and zero writes occurred (FR-006, research §6).

bindings.description: Applied bindings, ordered by spec_folder ascending, then feature before story, then story_ordinal ascending. Order is total and deterministic so both ports emit identical bytes; it never depends on the order Jira returned results (FR-012).

story_ordinal.description: Non-null exactly when level = story; the ordinal the bridge already assigns to the user story in spec.md.

reason.description: FR-024 — why this candidate was chosen. There is no third value: FR-012 forbids any similarity, order, recency, or issue-type heuristic from existing in any code path.

overrode_key.description: FR-022 — non-null only when an explicit binding overrode a discovered candidate; carries the discovered key that was overridden, so the plan states both.

status.description: `adopt` emits exactly one identity stamp. `already-adopted` emits NO action: the ticket already carries this spec's marker with origin human, so it is skipped rather than re-stamped and counted as skipped (FR-027) — which is what makes an interrupted adoption complete on re-run with exactly one stamp per ticket (SC-007).

refusals.description: Per-binding refusals. Each leaves zero writes for its binding while unambiguous bindings in the same run still apply, and any refusal makes the run exit 4 (FR-013). Same ordering rule as `bindings`.

reason.description: A CLOSED set, so the conformance corpus can assert one fixture per class (SC-005) and both ports cannot drift into differently-worded reasons (NFR-1). no-candidate: FR-009. several-candidates: FR-010. already-claimed / spec-owns-bridge-ticket: FR-011. wrong-project: FR-005. unbound-parent: FR-014. wrong-parent: FR-015. ambiguous-short-number: two spec folders in scope share the numbering component a short-form label names.

issue_keys.description: Every key involved, sorted ascending. For several-candidates this is ALL candidates, never a truncated pair — which is why discovery must paginate to exhaustion (NFR-6).

message.description: Names the spec folder and every ticket involved (Principle XVI). Carries no credential and no site host (FR-025).

remediation.description: A copy-pasteable command line. For no-candidate and several-candidates this is the `adopt --bind` invocation that resolves it — which is precisely why US4 is the documented answer to US2.

out_of_scope.description: FR-026 — spec folders excluded by --spec, sorted ascending. No label of theirs entered any query and no ticket of theirs was read or written.
